description:
Spec: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §Message/set, §Reaction.

Spec text: "Reactions are added/removed by patching reactions/{senderReactionId} as a JSON Pointer in Message/set update. Servers MUST set senderId: \"self\" on owner reactions; clients SHOULD only add/remove reactions where senderId is \"self\"; servers MUST reject otherwise with forbidden."

Current state: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/message.rs has no reaction-patch parsing. Message.reactions is a typed HashMap in jmap-chat-types but there is no Message/set update path that accepts patches against it. grep for "reaction" in chat-server/src returned 0 hits.

## Acceptance

- handle_message_set parses JSON Pointer patches of the form "reactions/{key}" where the value is a Reaction object (add) or JSON null (remove)
- Server overrides sender_id to SenderId::Owner on every add, regardless of what the client supplied (defense in depth; spec MUST)
- Server rejects update if any reaction patch targets a key the caller did not author (senderId != "self" on existing reaction): SetError::Forbidden
- Backend write goes through whatever existing update_object path message/set already uses (no new ChatBackend method)
- Unit test: client patches reactions/abc with {emoji:"👍"} — succeeds, stored Reaction has sender_id == Owner
- Unit test: client patches reactions/foo with null where reactions[foo].sender_id == "someoneElse" — rejected forbidden
- Unit test: client patches reactions/bar with {emoji:"❤️", senderId:"someone"} — succeeds but stored sender_id == Owner (server overrode)

## Out of scope

- Federated reaction delivery (Peer/deliver reactionUpdate) — federation spec, deferred to Layer E
- Custom emoji validation (a separate path)
title: Layer A: Parse reaction patches in Message/set update (reactions/{senderReactionId} JSON Pointer)
